title: Alectinib monotherapy
context_label: ALK-positive NSCLC · adjuvant or advanced disease
scope_note: This guide covers alectinib alone for ALK-positive lung cancer. Confirm whether it is adjuvant treatment after complete surgery, first treatment for advanced cancer, or treatment after crizotinib. These settings have different evidence and treatment lengths.
indication_text: Alectinib targets an abnormal ALK growth signal. After complete surgery the aim is to reduce the chance of cancer returning; in advanced cancer the aim is to control the cancer. Your team explains the individual aim, alternatives and uncertainty.
purpose: Alectinib targets an abnormal ALK growth signal. After complete surgery the aim is to reduce the chance of cancer returning; in advanced cancer the aim is to control the cancer. Your team explains the individual aim, alternatives and uncertainty.
schedule_summary: Take alectinib twice daily with food, every day, with no planned rest week. After surgery, treatment lasts up to 24 months, stopping sooner for recurrence or unacceptable side effects. For advanced cancer, treatment continues until progression or unacceptable side effects under the oncology plan.
administration_text: The usual starting dose is 600 mg twice daily: four 150 mg capsules each time, taken with food. Use your own prescription, which may specify a lower dose. Swallow capsules whole; do not open or dissolve them. If a dose is missed, take it only if the next dose is more than 6 hours away. If the next dose is due within 6 hours, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses together. If you vomit after a dose, take the next dose at its usual time; do not take an extra dose.
monitoring_summary: Liver profile every 2 weeks for the first 3 months, then every 4 weeks or as clinically indicated. FBC and renal profile every 4 weeks. CPK every 2 weeks for the first month, then as clinically indicated, including muscle symptoms. Blood pressure and pulse as clinically indicated. NCCP says ECG prior to cycle 2, then as indicated; a continuous oral regimen has no defined cycle length, so agree the first repeat ECG appointment locally. Assess symptoms, interactions, adherence, current dose and treatment benefit; scans and disease monitoring follow the Consultant plan.

agents.name: Alectinib
agents.mechanism: Blocks an abnormal ALK growth signal
agents.explanation: Alectinib blocks the abnormal ALK protein that drives growth in ALK-positive cancer cells. It can act against cancer in the body and brain. It can also affect healthy tissues, so blood tests and symptom checks remain important.
agents.watch: Take with food. Keep blood tests and report muscle weakness, breathing changes, jaundice or dizziness promptly.
risks: Muscle pain or weakness and raised CPK
Liver injury and raised liver tests or bilirubin
Anaemia, including destruction of red blood cells (haemolysis)
Slow heart rate, dizziness or fainting
Lung inflammation (ILD/pneumonitis), which can be serious
Skin rash and sensitivity to sunlight
Gastrointestinal perforation; urgent severe abdominal pain
Potential harm to a developing baby

safety_note: Keep your oncology emergency number available. A serious symptom needs review between scheduled visits.
urgent_extra: Contact the oncology team promptly for new or worsening cough or breathlessness, unexplained muscle pain or weakness, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, marked tiredness or pallor, dizziness or fainting, severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or reduced urine. Sudden serious breathing difficulty, severe chest pain or collapse needs emergency help. Do not wait for the next blood test.

You can ask for an interpreter, more time or another explanation and can reconsider. This aid supports a consent conversation; it does not replace it.

chronology_notes.title: Early checks
chronology_notes.text: Liver tests every 2 weeks for 3 months; CPK every 2 weeks for the first month.

chronology_notes.title: Continuous dosing

chronology_notes.title: ECG timing
chronology_notes.text: Ask when the first repeat ECG is booked. NCCP uses the phrase prior to cycle 2 without defining an oral cycle length.

support.title: Anti-sickness medicines
support.text: Alectinib is minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Treat nausea with prescribed as-required medicine if needed. Routine preventive anti-sickness treatment and infusion premedication are not required; your team selects a suitable rescue medicine.

support.title: Capsules, food and missed doses
support.text: The usual starting dose is 600 mg twice daily: four 150 mg capsules each time, taken with food. Use your own prescription, which may specify a lower dose. Swallow capsules whole; do not open or dissolve them. If a dose is missed, take it only if the next dose is more than 6 hours away. If the next dose is due within 6 hours, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses together. If you vomit after a dose, take the next dose at its usual time; do not take an extra dose.

support.title: Muscles, liver, blood and breathing
support.text: Keep liver, CPK and blood-count appointments. Muscle symptoms, jaundice, dark urine, unusual fatigue, cough or breathlessness need prompt review even between appointments.

support.title: Heart rate and other medicines
support.text: Tell the team about dizziness, fainting and medicines that slow the pulse. Check new prescriptions, supplements, grapefruit and Seville oranges with pharmacy; interactions may require closer monitoring rather than an automatic dose change.

support.title: Sun protection
support.text: Avoid prolonged sunlight during treatment and for at least 7 days after stopping. Use broad-spectrum UVA/UVB sunscreen and lip balm SPF 50 or higher.

support.title: Pregnancy, contraception and breastfeeding
support.text: Women who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least 5 weeks afterwards. Men with female partners who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months afterwards. Oral contraceptive effectiveness may be reduced: ask for a suitable method. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility before treatment and contact the team promptly if pregnancy occurs.

passport_visit_note: Use the passport for ongoing oral treatment reviews. The number of recording pages is not a prescribed duration. Record dose changes, missed doses and symptoms; do not use it to authorise your own dose.
anatomy_note: Possible effects do not predict what will happen to you. Symptoms can have other causes and need assessment.
anatomy: Report promptly because lung inflammation can occur.
A slow pulse can be symptomatic and needs medicine review.
Liver injury may start silently; keep tests and report yellow skin or dark urine.
Anaemia can include red-cell breakdown; report marked changes.
CPK tests help assess muscle injury; report unexplained symptoms.
Use high-factor sun protection during treatment and for 7 days after stopping.

sections.title: Supply and visits
sections.text: Request the next supply before capsules run out. Blood tests and ECGs need their own appointments. Alectinib itself does not require a line or infusion pump.

sections.title: A hold or dose change
sections.text: Ask what is held, what needs to recover and who will authorise restarting. Do not restart or change the dose yourself.

evidence.title: Evidence differs after surgery and in advanced cancer
evidence.intro: Studies describe groups in a particular setting. Ask which comparison applies to you.
evidence.population: Completely resected ALK-positive NSCLC; untreated advanced ALK-positive NSCLC; or advanced cancer after crizotinib, studied separately.
evidence.interpretation: After complete surgery, ALINA found that alectinib delayed cancer recurrence compared with platinum chemotherapy; whether it improves overall survival remains uncertain. In untreated advanced cancer, ALEX showed better cancer control than crizotinib, but its final survival comparison did not establish a clear overall-survival difference. Separate studies showed tumour responses after crizotinib. These groups cannot predict your personal outcome or rank all current treatment choices.
evidence.limitations: The after-surgery study does not yet establish a survival benefit. Advanced-disease trials do not compare every modern ALK medicine. Group averages do not predict an individual result.

chapters.title: Before the first capsules
chapters.intro: Confirm a practical plan with your team.

items.title: Baseline checks
items.text: Confirm ALK-positive NSCLC by a validated test; establish indication, staging/resection and prior-treatment history. FBC, renal and liver profile, CPK, blood pressure and ECG before treatment. Review all medicines, supplements, muscle/lung/cardiac symptoms, pregnancy, contraception and breastfeeding. For treatment after crizotinib allow a minimum 7-day washout. For adjuvant treatment confirm complete resection, high-risk criteria and ECOG 0–1.

items.title: Oral treatment and access
items.text: Confirm the prescription and supply route. Adjuvant use is listed in NCCP, but the printed reimbursement field is N/A; the team checks current access separately.

items.title: Medicines and food
items.text: Check all prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal products with pharmacy. Ask specifically about medicines that slow the pulse and grapefruit/Seville oranges. Do not stop another prescribed medicine on your own.

items.text: Discuss benefit, side effects and priorities at reviews. After planned adjuvant completion, agree the ongoing lung-cancer follow-up plan.

questions.q: Does taking capsules mean fewer important risks?
questions.a: Capsules are cancer treatment and can cause serious side effects. Keep the planned tests and use the oncology contact plan for new symptoms.

questions.q: Does having side effects show it is working?
questions.a: No. Side effects do not reliably indicate cancer response; your team assesses benefit using the relevant follow-up plan.

questions.q: How long will I take alectinib?
questions.a: Take alectinib twice daily with food, every day, with no planned rest week. After surgery, treatment lasts up to 24 months, stopping sooner for recurrence or unacceptable side effects. For advanced cancer, treatment continues until progression or unacceptable side effects under the oncology plan.

questions.q: What if I miss a dose or vomit?
questions.a: If a dose is missed, take it only if the next dose is more than 6 hours away. If the next dose is due within 6 hours, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses together. If you vomit after a dose, take the next dose at its usual time; do not take an extra dose.
Liver tests are planned every 2 weeks for 3 months. CPK is checked every 2 weeks for the first month. Blood count and kidney tests are checked every 4 weeks; symptoms may prompt extra tests.
NCCP asks for an ECG before its second treatment cycle, but this medicine is taken continuously. Ask the team to confirm the first repeat ECG appointment and later checks.

questions.q: Can I change or restart my dose myself?
questions.a: No. If alectinib is held or reduced, ask what needs to recover, when review happens and who will authorise restarting.

questions.q: What should I say when calling?
questions.a: Give the medicine name, current dose, last dose, symptoms and when they began. Explain whether you can drink, pass urine and manage usual activities. Do not delay calling to collect details.

questions.q: Can I use this page to decide whether tests are safe?
questions.a: No. Blood results, symptoms, current dose and treatment history need the prescriber’s assessment. This guide does not authorise treatment.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates?
questions.a: No. This map shows general timing. Your hospital arranges actual appointments.
